issues.detail: Missing coverage of logout handling, token revocation endpoints, operational key rotation contingencies, CORS handling, and comprehensive edge cases like token blacklisting strategies.
Examples and key generation guidance are locked to Node.js/jsonwebtoken; no demonstrations for Python, Go, Java, or other platforms advertised as compatible.
Only two examples provided, one of which is a debugging scenario; missing runnable code for token validation middleware implementation and key rotation procedures.

scenarios.name: jwt-validation-middleware
scenarios.rationale: Response B directly implements the rubric's required error codes (token_missing, token_expired, token_invalid) and maps TokenExpiredError/JsonWebTokenError exactly as specified; Response A uses different codes (MISSING_TOKEN, TOKEN_EXPIRED, MALFORMED_TOKEN, etc.) and doesn't collapse JsonWebTokenError variants to token_invalid, failing the core error-mapping requirement despite offering more granular error handling.

scenarios.name: refresh-token-rotation
scenarios.rationale: Both fully implement all four rubric requirements (revoke-before-issue, family ID assignment/reuse, token hashing, replay detection with family revocation). Response B edges ahead with additional security layers (generation tracking, out-of-order detection), cleaner status enum pattern, forensic data capture (userAgent/IP), explicit test scenarios, and NestJS alignment with the project's backend stack; Response A excels in completeness with full client-side integration and Express patterns, but the framework choice is less aligned with the project context.

scenarios.name: jwt-expiration-debug
scenarios.rationale: Both responses correctly decode the JWT and identify the expired token; Response A fully addresses the refresh-token recommendation with concrete implementation details and correctly identifies the lifetime as 1 hour (longer than best-practice 15 minutes), while Response B calculates the same 1-hour lifetime but undermines the recommendation by suggesting 24h+ TTLs (worse practice) and provides less actionable guidance on refresh implementation.
